questiontext.text:
Goal

A goal log stores the score from every football match in a season. Add a new five-a-side result to the club's log and calculate the season total.

Read
  • Go Slices: usage and internals. In "Growing slices (the copy and append functions)", find the append signature. What type does it return? Check the two following examples and the final Filter example. Where does each example store the returned value? What does Filter declare before its loop?
  • On the same page, find "Slices" and the sentence about a slice's zero value. What do len and cap return for that value?
  • For statements with range clause. Find the table row for a slice. What is the first iteration value? What is the second?
Coming from Java

In Java, goals.add(3) returns nothing and changes the list in place. An enhanced for loop provides each element but not its position.

List<Integer> goals = new ArrayList<>();
goals.add(3);
for (int g : goals) total += g;
Required: append
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Find the Filter example at the end of Growing slices. Use the form of the line that grows its result.
  • In the range table, which iteration value does a loop with one variable receive?

testcode.text: var goals []int goals = record(goals, 4) goals = record(goals, 0) fmt.Println(goals, len(goals), season(goals))

questiontext.text:
Goal

A warehouse has a fixed number of shelves, but a delivery can contain any number of boxes. When a delivery does not fit, the night crew builds a larger warehouse and moves the existing stock into it. Make room for every delivery without losing stock.

Read
  • make. Read the Slice line. What does the second integer argument set? What does make([]int, 0, 10) return?
  • append. Read the first three sentences. What happens when the destination has enough capacity? What happens when its capacity is too small?
  • Passing arguments to ... parameters. Read the opening paragraph. Inside the function, what type does a final ...T parameter have? What does it hold if the call supplies no arguments? In the final example, what does the call with s... pass?
Coming from Java

In Java, new ArrayList<>(shelves) sets a capacity that the list does not report. The size() method reports the element count. Go reports both numbers.

List<String> stock = new ArrayList<>(shelves);
stock.addAll(List.of(boxes));
Required: make
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Find the make example where the array and slice have different sizes. Which number corresponds to shelves?
  • Find the type of boxes in the specification. The second append example shows how one call passes a complete slice.

testcode.text: w := newWarehouse(0) fmt.Println(len(w), spare(w)) w = store(w, "bolts", "nuts") fmt.Println(w, len(w))
w := newWarehouse(0) delivery := []string{"nuts", "washers"} w = store(w, "bolts") w = store(w, delivery...) fmt.Println(w, len(w))
w := newWarehouse(3) fmt.Println(w, len(w), spare(w)) w = store(w) fmt.Println(len(w), spare(w))
w := newWarehouse(4) w = store(w, "bolts", "nuts") same := store(w, "washers") grown := store(same, "screws", "rivets") fmt.Println(cap(same) == cap(w), cap(grown) == cap(w), len(grown), spare(same))

questiontext.text:
Goal

A row of cards stays in place while the dealer selects different sections of it. A cut, a hand, and a reveal each refer to part of the same row. reveal shows the first n cards from where a hand starts in the row. Do not stop at the hand's own length, because the row behind it may hold more cards.

Read
  • Slice expressions. Under "Simple slice expressions", find the example with a := [5]int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. What are the length and capacity of s? What is the default low index? What is the default high index?
  • In the same section, find the sentence beginning "For slices, the upper index bound". What is the bound? Find the paragraph beginning "If the sliced operand". What does a non-nil result share with its operand?
  • Slice types. Find the sentence about integer indexes for slice elements. Which indexes are valid? In the last paragraph, what can differ between inner slices? What must you initialise separately?
Coming from Java

In Java, deck.subList(from, to) throws when to exceeds the list size. A Java developer might also make a defensive copy of the result. Go gives to a different bound, and this task forbids a copy.

List<String> top = new ArrayList<>(deck.subList(0, at));
Banned: append
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Build the outer slice with make from WAT 09.2. Fill each inner slice by index.
  • Before adding a guard to reveal, check the upper index bound for slices.

testcode.text: deck := []string{"A", "K", "Q", "J", "10"} top, rest := cut(deck, 1) fmt.Println(len(top), cap(top), len(rest), cap(rest)) none, all := cut(deck, 0) whole, empty := cut(deck, 5) fmt.Println(len(none), all, whole, len(empty))
